title: Machine learning identifies IgA nephropathy subgroups that benefit from immunosuppression
summary: Using clinical and pathological data from 4047 biopsy-proven IgA nephropathy patients at 24 Chinese centres (derivation 2058, validation 1989), model-based recursive partitioning found three subgroups with long-term immunosuppression benefit for kidney failure. Examples are creatinine at most 1.437 mg/dl with proteinuria above 2.480 g/24h (HR 0.23) and, at higher creatinine, high proteinuria with crescents (HR 0.29). The benefits were externally validated in the validation cohort; the data are retrospective and observational, and recursive partitioning is a borderline machine learning method.
ai_technology: Model-based recursive partitioning, a machine learning method, partitioning patients by immunosuppression benefit
organization: Nanjing General Hospital of Nanjing Military Command; Nanjing University

evidence.tested: Subgroup treatment effects found in the derivation cohort were checked in a validation cohort of 1989 patients.
evidence.unknown: Whether the subgroup benefits hold in a randomized trial, given confounding in observational data; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Recursive partitioning identified patient subgroups with different immunosuppression benefit.
